  Building a table image of an opponent is difficult
for inexperienced players. To learn this skill, start by
concentrating on a single player at your table. The player
to your immediate right is an ideal choice as you will have
position on them in nearly all of the hands, which gives
you a permanent advantage over them and allows you to
play more pots with them. Start by assessing how many
hands they are open raising so you can accurately define
what their range is. Follow up by assessing how often they
fold to three-bets in each position. If they fold most of the
time, you can widen your three-bet bluff range. Stop bluff-
ing them if they never fold and widen your value range.
